html:
The United States has completed its full withdrawal of forces from Iraq after more than two decades, ending its mission and leaving the country's defense future uncertain, as Trump simultaneously warns that the U.S. "may blow up" Iran or reach a deal with it very soon.

Global Security & Diplomacy: A dramatic aviation security incident unfolded on a Flydubai flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv, where a pilot allegedly stabbed another and attempted to crash the plane. Passengers and crew reportedly subdued the attacker, leading to an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia. Israel's Prime Minister praised the landing pilot as a "hero" and labeled the event a "terrorist attack attempt." Flydubai has suspended flights to Israel as investigations proceed. This coincided with significant US-Iran diplomatic friction, with a senior American official demanding the Iranian Foreign Minister leave the U.S. Iran also indicated receipt of a US response to its latest offer to end a war, while its nuclear program enters a critical phase as Tehran debates dropping out of a non-proliferation treaty.

European Fronts: Russia has launched its heaviest combined assault on Ukraine’s energy infrastructure in months, resulting in seven fatalities and triggering emergency power cuts across Kyiv and surrounding regions. The attacks highlight a difficult winter ahead for Ukraine, with Putin reportedly showing no signs of stopping the war. Concurrently, UK PM Burnham has reopened the divisive debate on Britain rejoining the EU, breaking a taboo and sending a message that being outside the EU has been "pretty cold." Separately, student protests have escalated in France, leading to hundreds of arrests and dozens of injuries.

Global Economy & Markets: Major corporations, including Microsoft’s datacentre business, Optus parent Singtel, and Netflix, are under scrutiny for reportedly paying minimal or zero income tax on billion-dollar revenues in Australia. In the media sector, a federal judge has approved Paramount’s takeover of Warner Bros. Discovery, clearing antitrust challenges and including safeguards for CNN’s editorial independence.

North American Affairs: Domestically, the US faced a halted execution as Christa Pike was reportedly heard snoring 40 minutes after lethal doses were administered, with her condition unclear, after the US Supreme Court allowed her execution to go ahead. California has banned child marriage and enacted laws protecting workers from AI threats, including potential job losses and workplace surveillance. US President Donald Trump renewed calls for former Federal Reserve chief Jerome Powell's resignation and ordered agencies to use "Super Intelligence" instead of AI. Separately, a man was arrested over an alleged plot to attack the Texas state capitol.

Environmental, Social & Regional Shifts: Swiss glaciers suffered a "disastrous" year of ice loss, with over 5% of their ice volume vanishing this year alone, threatening water supplies across Europe. In India's Balaghat district, at least 32 children have died since May amid measles and malaria outbreaks. El Salvador has set 2027 presidential elections, paving the way for Nayib Bukele to seek a third term following constitutional changes. Five EU states are moving forward with plans to establish their first deportation center in Africa by 2027, while Japan officially overhauled its permanent residency rules, raising fees for foreign nationals.
